key_insight: A psychiatry-specialized LLM (PsychFound) fine-tuned on expert knowledge and de-identified clinical records achieves clinical-grade performance and improves diagnostic and treatment decisions when integrated into psychiatric workflows.
problem_solved: General-purpose LLMs lack domain-specific knowledge, clinical reasoning alignment, and workflow integration needed for safe, reliable psychiatric decision support.
method: Domain-adaptive training: pretraining/finetuning on curated psychiatric guidelines, textbooks, and expert annotations.
Clinical exposure: additional fine-tuning on de-identified electronic health records and case notes to teach real-world presentation and documentation patterns.
Safety and evaluation: multi-objective optimization for diagnostic accuracy, treatment guideline adherence, and risk mitigation, validated against clinical benchmarks and workflow trials.
impact: Demonstrates that targeted domain adaptation plus clinical data can yield LLMs suitable for high-stakes medical support; a blueprint for practitioners to build, evaluate, and safely deploy specialty LLMs with human-in-the-loop oversight.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: pipeline showing expert-knowledge corpus → clinical-record fine-tuning → safety alignment → deployed model.
Performance chart: bar/line chart comparing PsychFound vs baseline LLMs and clinician benchmarks on diagnostic accuracy, guideline adherence, and safety metrics.
Clinical workflow schematic: how model outputs integrate into clinician decision-making (e.g., suggestions, explanations, risk flags) with human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
Case vignette panel: side-by-side example of model-assisted vs unaided clinician decisions with outcome annotations.
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
